answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring continuous proof of a unique computational path across a mesa of shared verification nodes. Each agent must carry a private sparrow-like lightweight state that only converges correctly at relic checkpoints tied to their key. An attacker forging multiple identities must either replicate isolated mesa computations for every clone (paying full verification cost per fake) or risk collision at relic points that invalidates all related bonds, making large-scale sybil farms economically unviable compared to honest single agents.
